question:
Two thin convex lenses $L_1$ and $L_2$ of focal lengths $f_1=10\,\text{cm}$ and $f_2=20\,\text{cm}$ are placed coaxially in air with separation $(f_1+f_2)$. An object consists of two very close point sources separated by a distance $s$ (perpendicular to the common principal axis) and is placed in the front focal plane of $L_1$. A screen is placed in the back focal plane of $L_2$.

Assume both lenses are aberration-free and the **only** factor limiting the sharpness/resolution on the screen is diffraction at the circular aperture of $L_2$ of diameter $D=2.0\,\text{cm}$. Monochromatic light of wavelength $\lambda=550\,\text{nm}$ is used.

Using Rayleigh criterion, find the minimum separation $s_{\min}$ between the two point sources so that their images are just resolved on the screen.
